newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn rules out early sell-off of airport stakes.
newsitem.headline: Bonn rules out early sell-off of airport stakes.

text.p: Germany has no plans to speed up privatisation of its airport shareholdings to ease government finances, the country's transport ministry said.
Bonn had not fixed a timescale for its planned sale of holdings in five German airports and had made no estimates of potential revenue from the sale, a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Under a 1994 air transport strategy, the German state plans to dispose of 26 percent stakes in Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg and Munich airports and of a 31 percent holding in Cologne/Bonn airport.
"There is no Cabinet decision on when privatisation could take place and there is no fixed timescale at the moment," the spokesman said.
"Hamburg is the most advanced and could happen in the next 2-3 years," he added.

Transport state secretary Hans-Jochen Henke told representatives of the five airports in question and of the finance ministry at a meeting late Tuesday that privatisation would keep German airports internationally competitive, a ministry statement said.
A proposed cooperation network of German airports should aim to be more cost-effective, improve capacity usage and increase competitiveness, Henke said.
Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said on May 23 it favoured the establishment of a German airports alliance under its leadership with FAG stakes in other airports, including Duesseldorf.

The German airports association (ADV), representing all 16 international airports in Germany, has been commissioned to analyse the competitive situation of German airports and to draw up cooperation models, the transport ministry said.
These suggestions would be discussed in the second half of the year, it added.

* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 22.34 points, or 0.6 percent, to 3,313.71.
Bourse volume was at 2.41 billion francs.
One dealer said there was some profit-taking in financials, whereas industrials were generally lifted by a firming dollar.

* Bank shares were surrounded by recurring rumours of takeovers, spin-offs, mergers and restructuring, dealers said. UBS bearers fell 10 francs to 1,591, while most-active CS Holding jumped seven francs, or 3.76 percent, to a closing high of 193.25.
* Novartis registered shares were among the few losers among blue chips. The stocks ended down one franc at 1,987 due to profit taking. Roche was up 125 francs at 13,160.

* Alusuisse ended with a gain of six francs to 1,396 after surging to an all-time high of 1,414 francs in early trade. Old rumours regarding a possible spin-off of one of Alusuisse's units led to soaring demand, dealers said.
* Sulzer, Holderbank, Ciba and Baloise were among the biggest winners among blue chips.
* On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), trade was generally quiet.

Options of CS Group were in demand, which was reflective of the stock's rise on the cash market, one dealer said. Of the total 136,379 options traded, CS Group accounted for nearly 39,000 calls and 3,142 puts.
On the futures side, 4,664 SMI futures changed hands. The June SMI futures were up 35.5 points to 5,212.5.
